item.title: Nepal condemns attacks on civilians after citizen killed by drone debris at Saudi oil field
item.description: Nepal has expressed sadness over the death of a Nepali citizen killed by debris from an intercepted drone near Saudi Aramco’s Shaybah oil field. Two expatriates were killed, while Pakistani and Indian ...
item.content:encoded:
Nepal condemns attacks on civilians after citizen killed by drone debris at Saudi oil field Nepal has expressed sadness over the death of a Nepali citizen killed by debris from an intercepted drone near Saudi Aramco’s Shaybah oil field. Two expatriates were killed, while Pakistani and Indian nationals were injured. Nepal condemned attacks on civilians and critical infrastructure. ANI | Updated: 23-10-2026 10:13 IST | Created: 23-10-2026 10:13 IST

Representative Image (Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Nepal's Ministry of Foreign Affairs expressed deep sadness over the death of a Nepali citizen in Saudi Arabia. According to the ministry, the person was killed by debris from a drone that Saudi air defence systems intercepted over Saudi Aramco's Shaybah oil field a day earlier. In a statement posted on X, the ministry offered condolences to the bereaved family and wished a speedy recovery to all those injured. It reiterated Nepal's "unequivocal condemnation" of attacks targeting civilians and critical infrastructure. The ministry said Nepal continues to call for the peaceful resolution of disputes through dialogue, negotiation and diplomatic engagement, which it described as the country's principled position. The statement did not name the victim, give his hometown or say whether arrangements were under way to repatriate his body. Saudi Arabia's Ministry of Energy said air defence systems intercepted a drone attempting to target one of the oil field's processing facilities in the Eastern Province on Wednesday morning. The attempted attack caused a fire in a contractor's vehicle outside the facility's perimeter, without affecting operations. The ministry said two expatriates, one Nepali and one Filipino, were killed, while a Pakistani and an Indian national were injured. Saudi Arabia is a major destination for Nepali migrant workers, thousands of whom are employed across the country. The Saudi ministry's statement did not identify who launched the drone. The incident came amid a series of drone and missile attacks on Saudi Arabia attributed to Yemen's Houthi rebels. The United States ordered non-emergency embassy staff and their families to leave Saudi Arabia on Wednesday. Shaybah produces around one million barrels of crude oil a day and is located close to the border with the United Arab Emirates. The field was also targeted in March, when Saudi forces said they had shot down ten drones heading towards it. The foreign ministry did not say whether it had contacted the family or Saudi authorities, or what consular support it would provide. Nepal's embassy in Riyadh and the Department of Foreign Employment have not yet commented publicly. (ANI)

item.title: Tom Cruise to receive 52nd AFI Life Achievement Award
item.description: The award will be given by the American Film Institute at a gala tribute, in a ceremony set to be held at the Dolby Theatre in Hollywood on April 24, 2027.
item.content:encoded:
Tom Cruise to receive 52nd AFI Life Achievement Award  The award will be given by the American Film Institute at a gala tribute, in a ceremony set to be held at the Dolby Theatre in Hollywood on April 24, 2027. ANI | Updated: 23-10-2026 10:12 IST | Created: 23-10-2026 10:12 IST

Actor Tom Cruise (File photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Hollywood actor Tom Cruise has been selected to be bestowed with the 52nd AFI Life Achievement Award, Variety reported. The award will be given by the American Film Institute at a gala tribute, in a ceremony set to be held at the Dolby Theatre in Hollywood on April 24, 2027. Considered the highest honour for a career in film, the AFI Life Achievement Award is given to a single honouree every year, recognising talent that has furthered the cinematic arts, demonstrated longevity and been acknowledged by scholars, critics, peers, and audiences. Speaking on the same, Chair of the AFI Board of Trustees Kathleen Kennedy shared, “Tom Cruise is a global icon. As an actor and producer, he brings an extraordinary commitment to everything he does. What I especially admire is his deep belief in movies and their ability to bring people together.” Kennedy added, “That passion has made him an extraordinary ambassador for American film around the world. It is AFI’s honour to present him with the 52nd AFI Life Achievement Award,” as quoted by Variety. In a career spanning over five decades, Tom Cruise – a renowned actor, producer, and philanthropist has several hit titles to his name, including ‘Top Gun’, ‘Risky Business’, ‘Minority Report’, ‘Interview with the Vampire’, ‘A Few Good Men’, and the popular ‘Mission: Impossible’ films. He will be seen next in the next chapter of ‘Days of Thunder’ alongside Anne Hathaway. Cruise also received several accolades in his career, including Best Actor nods for his work on ‘Born on the Fourth of July’ and ‘Jerry Maguire’. He recently won a nomination as a producer of ‘Top Gun: Maverick’, which was also nominated for Best Picture. (ANI)

item.title: "Iran doing everything to drive up oil prices ahead of midterms": Trump lashes out at Tehran regime
item.description: US President Donald Trump launched a blistering attack against Tehran, accusing the Iranian leadership of manufacturing crises to artificially hike global crude oil prices ahead of the upcoming United ...
item.content:encoded:
"Iran doing everything to drive up oil prices ahead of midterms": Trump lashes out at Tehran regime US President Donald Trump launched a blistering attack against Tehran, accusing the Iranian leadership of manufacturing crises to artificially hike global crude oil prices ahead of the upcoming United States midterm elections and reaffirming that Iran must never be allowed to acquire nuclear capabilities. ANI | Updated: 23-10-2026 10:11 IST | Created: 23-10-2026 10:11 IST

US President Donald Trump (Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

US President Donald Trump launched a blistering attack against Tehran, accusing the Iranian leadership of manufacturing crises to artificially hike global crude oil prices ahead of the upcoming United States midterm elections and reaffirming that Iran must never be allowed to acquire nuclear capabilities. In a sharply worded post shared across his social media channels, Trump dismissed allegations of major disruptions in the Persian Gulf, asserting that oil shipments through the critical maritime corridor remain elevated. "Iran is doing everything they can to drive up the price of Oil prior to the U.S. Midterm Election. They are even making up fake hits, mines, and everything else, because more Oil is coming through the Hormuz Strait now than it did even prior to the beginning of the Conflict," Trump said. Labelling the dispensation in Tehran an "evil regime", Trump accused authorities of carrying out brutal, lethal crackdowns against civilian protesters on a mass scale. "They continue to kill protestors, and anyone else that happens to be in their way. It is truly an Evil Regime, and I can only hope the American Public, and the World, understands how EVIL they are! 75,000 protestors lie dead in less than seven months," the US President claimed. Lashing out at domestic political opponents and the broader international community for what he termed an indifferent posture, Trump drew a firm red line regarding Tehran's atomic program. "It is shocking how the World, and the Dumocrat Party, seem not to care. IRAN CAN NEVER HAVE A NUCLEAR WEAPON, AND THEY WILL NEVER A NUCLEAR WEAPON!" Trump wrote. Meanwhile, the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) Navy issued a warning to the United States over what it described as efforts to encourage vessels to pass through a mined maritime passage. In a statement attributed to the IRGC Navy Command, the force accused Washington of encouraging ships to navigate the passage despite the presence of mines and warned that continued actions could widen the confrontation to US military bases in the region. "The arrogant US regime's insistence on inciting vessels to pass through the illegally mined passage has increased maritime accidents day by day, and the aggressive US military should know that if this trend continues, the scope of the confrontation will extend to the aggressive bases in the region. This is a serious warning," the IRGC Navy Command said. The statement comes as Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) Navy has claimed that it struck and set fire to four ships carrying oil cargoes in the northern Persian Gulf, while three other vessels collided with mines in the western Strait of Hormuz, according to Iranian state media, Islamic Republic of Iran Broadcasting (IRIB). In a statement issued on Thursday, the IRGC Navy said the four ships had previously crossed an "illegal route" despite warnings to the maritime companies operating them. Earlier, US President Donald Trump on Wednesday (local time) said that the United States is not negotiating with Iran and "something" will happen "fairly soon." (ANI)

item.title: US orders removal of China’s DeepSeek AI over national security concerns
item.description: The US government ordered federal agencies to remove DeepSeek AI applications from government systems, citing national security risks, data exposure concerns, and potential ties to Chinese authorities ...
item.content:encoded:
US orders removal of China’s DeepSeek AI over national security concerns The US government ordered federal agencies to remove DeepSeek AI applications from government systems, citing national security risks, data exposure concerns, and potential ties to Chinese authorities. The directives also ban federal departments from using DeepSeek technology in official operations and contracts. ANI | Updated: 22-10-2026 19:05 IST | Created: 22-10-2026 19:05 IST

Representative Image (File Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

The United States has directed federal agencies to remove applications developed by Chinese artificial intelligence company DeepSeek from government computer systems, citing potential national security risks and concerns over the exposure of sensitive information to Chinese authorities, The Epoch Times reported. The restrictions also prohibit federal departments from using DeepSeek technology in official operations and government contracts. According to The Epoch Times, the directives were issued on October 16 by the secretaries of Homeland Security and War, along with the director of national intelligence, under a federal law aimed at addressing security threats associated with government supply chains. A spokesperson for the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) told The Epoch Times that executive agencies are prohibited from installing, accessing or operating DeepSeek applications. Departments have also been instructed to identify and remove any existing installations from government systems. According to the report, the federal contracting database SAM.gov lists DeepSeek under an active exclusion effective October 16, without a specified expiration date. The Epoch Times reported that an earlier directive signed by the Department of Homeland Security on July 24 and made public on October 19 detailed the security concerns underlying the decision. According to The Epoch Times, the department warned that DeepSeek's servers are located in China, where authorities have extensive legal powers to access information held by private companies. This raises concerns that data submitted by American government employees and contractors could be transferred to China, potentially exposing confidential information about federal operations and personnel. Officials also flagged concerns about personal data collection, user tracking and cybersecurity vulnerabilities. In February 2025, cybersecurity firm NowSecure identified several weaknesses in DeepSeek's iPhone application, including unencrypted data transmission, insecure storage of sensitive information and features that could enable user tracking. Researchers also detected connections to infrastructure operated by ByteDance, the Chinese parent company of TikTok. The report said that a separate investigation by the House Select Committee on the Chinese Communist Party in April 2025 accused DeepSeek of transmitting American user data to China and aligning certain artificial intelligence responses with Beijing's censorship policies. (ANI)
